name: Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner — Ares Vallis

landing.solNote: sol count from landing (convention not sourced here)

scene.label: After Sojourner rolled onto the surface (NASA: 5 July 1997, US date; NSSDCA: ~05:40 UT 6 July). Local time ILLUSTRATIVE
scene.tauLabel: tau 0.5 ASSUMED (no sourced optical depth for this sol in the scene)

hardware.label: Mars Pathfinder lander (Carl Sagan Memorial Station)
hardware.provenance: DOCUMENTED RECONSTRUCTION — NASA publishes no 3D model. Tetrahedral lander, three solar petals with 2.8 m² of cells, IMP camera ~1.5 m above the ground, 1 m meteorology mast (Mars Pathfinder Landing Press Kit; NSSDCA). Petal size derived from the cell area; ramps and airbags ILLUSTRATIVE.

components.label: Imager for Mars Pathfinder (IMP) on its pop-up mast

hardware.label: Sojourner rover
hardware.provenance: DOCUMENTED RECONSTRUCTION — NASA publishes no 3D model. 65 x 48 x 30 cm, 10.6 kg, six 13 cm wheels, rocker-bogie, 0.2 m² solar array, APXS (Mars Pathfinder Landing Press Kit; NSSDCA gives 63 x 48 x 28 cm, 10.5 kg). Position just off the ramp ILLUSTRATIVE.

origin.registration: Catalogue coordinate; the hardware has NOT been identified in the HiRISE orthoimage yet. Historical coordinate frames can differ from the HiRISE/MOLA-controlled frame by up to hundreds of metres, so the true spot may be elsewhere in this terrain or beyond it.

terrain.dtm: USGS Astrogeology controlled HiRISE DTM DTEEC_002391_1995_001890_1995_A01 (collection mro_hirise_socet_dtms)
terrain.albedo: HiRISE orthoimage (RED band, single channel) at 0.5 m, colourised with an ILLUSTRATIVE soil ramp
terrain.horizon: same DTM, decimated to ~24 m, out to ~9 km where the DTM covers it
